quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to create more distance between your cars.
Brake hard to force them to back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors several times per minute to spot tailgaters or fast-approaching cars. If a car is following too closely, slow down and let it pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: Which of these directs drivers into the correct lanes for turning on some highways?

options.text: White lines on the side of the road
White arrows painted in the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows painted in the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows show which lanes are for specific uses, such as going straight or turning.

questions.question: When driving at night, slow down and:

options.text: Use high beams when no cars are coming toward you.
Wear sunglasses to reduce glare from other headlights.
Use high beams if it is also raining.
Turn on your interior light to see your speedometer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use high beams when no cars are coming toward you.
questions.explanation: By law, turn on your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise. Use high beams when no oncoming traffic is near.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit with extra caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down as soon as you see rain, snow, or sleet. These create slippery conditions. Safety may require driving slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Orange signs on highways are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Work zones are set up based on the type of work being done. Work zone signs are usually diamond-shaped, orange, and have black letters or symbols. They warn that people are working on or near the road.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a railroad crossing gate that is lowering or raising?

options.text: Yes, if an approaching train is far away.
Yes, if your vehicle can pass without hitting the gate.
Yes, if you look both ways first.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and/or bells at a railroad crossing mean stop completely. Do not cross the tracks until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully raised. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: An oncoming car is on your left and a bicyclist is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Split the difference and go between them.
Let the car pass, then pass the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: When there are multiple hazards, handle them one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist. Never try to squeeze between both at once.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Traffic only flows in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic only flows in the direction shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign shows the direction traffic must flow.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and get ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: If you are driving too slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Not let the other cars pass your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is unsafe. If traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane road, pull off the road and let other vehicles pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: Your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway, if possible.
Not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
Wait until the police arrive before moving your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway, if possible.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if you can. Always give your name and information at an accident scene.

questions.question: A train is approaching and could be dangerous. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find an alternative route across tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Always look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. Do not cross if a train is close enough or fast enough to be a danger. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are broken.

questions.question: Your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement. What should you do?

options.text: Immediately pull all the way off of the road and get back on when it is safe.
Accelerate and steer back on the road quickly.
Take your foot off the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator, slow down, then ease back onto the road when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Do not panic. Take your foot off the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the road with a small steering wheel turn. Keep both hands on the wheel and check for traffic before steering back onto the pavement.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon.
questions.explanation: Stop signs are the only eight-sided signs on the road. All octagon signs tell drivers to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: What is the safest way to drive in traffic?

options.text: Fluctuate your speed to keep alert.
Drive faster than the flow of traffic.
Drive slower than the flow of traffic.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go much faster or slower than other vehicles. Always drive with the flow of traffic while staying within the speed limit.

questions.question: Another car is coming toward you with bright headlights. What should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and then speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look away from the oncoming headlights and toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Be sure the passing lane is clear.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, make sure the passing lane is clear. Signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: One-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers which direction they must drive on a one-way street.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you not to enter the road or driveway ahead. If you see this sign, turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: Where should your car be positioned to make a right turn?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, move your car as far right as possible. Do not cut across other lanes to make your turn.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: No less safe than driving under any other conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely risky behavior.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Keeping your attention on driving helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes harmful gases from your vehicle. A leak allows carbon monoxide to enter the passenger area. Fix any exhaust leaks right away.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop your car?
questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road conditions have a major effect on how quickly you can stop. Slow down on slippery or poor roads to stay in control and be able to stop safely.
